entries.title: Cache friction factors in PipeFlowCalculator
entries.brief: Skip recomputing the friction factor for a flow already solved; results unchanged
entries.body:
## Goal

Stop `PipeFlowCalculator` from recomputing the friction factor for flows it has already solved.
A flow sweep, such as the `Slow` test `PipeFlowTests.DropGrowsMonotonicallyAcrossFlowSweep`, calls `IFrictionModel.FrictionFactor` once per point,
and the turbulent models spend most of their time in `Math.Pow` and `Math.Log10`.

This is a performance change only: every calculated result stays unchanged.

## Change

- Add `CachedFrictionModel : IFrictionModel` in `dotnet/src/LymCsharp.Hydraulics/CachedFrictionModel.cs`, a decorator over an inner `IFrictionModel`.
  - Below a Reynolds number of 2300 it calls the inner model directly; the laminar factor 64/Re is cheaper than a lookup.
  - At 2300 and above it rounds the Reynolds number to the nearest whole number and keys a `Dictionary<(double Reynolds, double RelativeRoughness), double>` on the rounded Reynolds number and the relative roughness.
    On a miss it computes the inner model's factor at the rounded Reynolds number and stores it, so an entry never depends on which caller filled it first.
  - It validates its arguments as the inner model does: a Reynolds number that is not positive throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`.
- `PipeFlowCalculator` wraps the model it is given in `CachedFrictionModel`, in both constructors, so every caller gets the cache without a code change.
- Keep `PipeFlowCalculator`'s public API as it is.

## Tests

- Add `dotnet/tests/LymCsharp.Hydraulics.Tests/CachedFrictionModelTests.cs`:
  - a second call with the same arguments does not reach the inner model (count calls on a stub model);
  - a laminar call always reaches the inner model;
  - a Reynolds number that is not positive throws.
- The existing `PipeFlowTests` and `FrictionTests` stay green unchanged.

entries.title: Add Quantity.Parse
entries.brief: Read a quantity back from the text Quantity.ToString writes
entries.body:
## Goal

Let callers read a quantity back from the text `Quantity.ToString` writes, such as `7.2 l/min` or `1.5 bar`, so a flow or pressure can come from a config file or a command line.

## Change

- Add `public static Quantity Parse(string text)` to `Quantity` in `dotnet/src/LymCsharp.Units/Quantity.cs`.
  - It reads a number, one space and a unit symbol, the form `Quantity.ToString` writes.
  - It looks the symbol up through `UnitRegistry.Find`, so an unknown symbol throws `KeyNotFoundException` as `Find` does.
  - Text with no space in it throws `FormatException`.
- Nothing else changes: no caller uses `Parse` yet, and no calculation or report output moves.

## Tests

Add to `dotnet/tests/LymCsharp.Units.Tests/QuantityTests.cs`:

- `Parse("1.5 bar")` gives the value 1.5 in `UnitCatalog.Bar`;
- `Parse("7.2 l/min")` gives the value 7.2 in `UnitCatalog.LitrePerMinute`;
- `Parse(q.ToString())` gives back `q` for a quantity such as 3.25 psi;
- an unknown symbol throws `KeyNotFoundException`;
- text with no space throws `FormatException`.

entries.title: Note transitional flow in the pipe flow report
entries.brief: Append a transitional-flow warning to the report line
entries.body:
## Goal

Warn the reader of a pipe flow report when the flow is transitional.
Between a Reynolds number of 2300 and 4000 no friction model is reliable, and the report line gives no sign of it.

## Change

- In `ResultFormatter.Format` (`dotnet/src/LymCsharp.Reporting/ResultFormatter.cs`), append ` (transitional: friction factor uncertain)` to the line when `result.Regime` is `FlowRegime.Transitional`.
  For example: `Transitional flow, v = 0.05 m/s, Re = 3000, dP = 0.1 psi (transitional: friction factor uncertain)`.
- Laminar and turbulent lines stay exactly as they are.
- Update the `Format` doc comment to name the note.

## Intended output change

This change moves regression output on purpose, in one place only:
the `report = …` line of each regression case whose flow is transitional gains the note.
Every other line of those cases, and every line of the laminar and turbulent cases, stays as it is.

## Tests

- Add a transitional case to `ResultFormatterTests.FormatsEveryValueToFourSignificantDigits`, or a test beside it, that expects the note.
- The existing laminar and turbulent cases stay unchanged.
